stories.label: Aramco building targeted after Saudi-led coalition hits Houthi site | The National
stories.summary: A missile set fire to a Saudi Aramco administrative building in Dhahran overnight, Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said, after a Saudi-led coalition strike on a Houthi site in Sanaa. The war has now reached the Eastern Province, home of the kingdom's oil industry, not only Riyadh's airport. Lead with the target, then the mechanism: Trump accused the Houthis of trying to push up oil prices 'at Iran's behest' before the US elections, and the reader should see what a strike near Aramco's headquarters does to Brent crude and to the war-risk premium on Gulf cargoes. Name the Yemeni civilians under the coalition strikes on Sanaa with the same weight as the Saudi side.

stories.label: Japan urges Russia for 'impartial treatment' of arrested journalist
stories.summary: Russia's FSB has charged Yuki Imai, a Hokkaido Shimbun reporter, with espionage after detaining him on Sakhalin, accusing him of gathering information on Moscow's defence capabilities for Tokyo. Lead with the charge and what it carries; the mechanism is a pattern: Russia has used espionage charges against foreign reporters (Evan Gershkovich) as leverage, and Japan, which sanctions Russia and arms Ukraine indirectly, has little to trade. Note Tokyo's muted wording, 'impartial treatment', against what it would say if an ally held its reporter.

stories.label: Trump's ambassador to Greece asked to resign amid misconduct allegations
stories.summary: Trump asked Kimberly Guilfoyle, US ambassador to Greece, to resign after reports that she sought $100,000 from a Trump supporter to pay personal credit-card debt and took luxury trips and hotel stays from wealthy Greek businessmen; she denies wrongdoing and has vowed to fight. Lead with the specific gifts and who gave them: the accountability question is what Greek business interests sought from the US embassy in Athens, a key post for East Med energy and arms deals. Dateline Athens.

stories.label: DR Congo Ebola cases pass 9,000 as efforts to curb transmission falter
stories.summary: The Health Ministry reports 9,066 confirmed Ebola cases and 4,381 deaths, a fatality rate near half, up from the 4,000 deaths reported on 2 October. Lead with the new count and the twelve-day rise. The mechanism: transmission is outrunning vaccination and contact tracing in Ituri and the east, where M23's advance and Kabila's new alliance with it fracture the state that would run the response. Name who funds the response and what has been cut.

stories.label: US fines Bank of America $1.2bn for money laundering, sanctions violations
stories.summary: The US Treasury imposed more than $1.21bn in penalties on Bank of America, the second-largest US bank, for anti-money-laundering and sanctions violations, including the third-largest penalty in the department's history. Lead with the size and with what the bank let through: which sanctioned parties and jurisdictions, over how many years, and how much money moved. The structural point: the same Treasury that enforces sanctions on others found its second-biggest bank processing the flows, and a fine is a fraction of a quarter's profit.

stories.label: Why the IMF is worried about a global debt squeeze as bond yields climb
stories.summary: New since yesterday's growth forecast: the IMF's fiscal warning that rising borrowing costs, with the US 10-year Treasury yield at a 24-year high, are straining public finances worldwide. Lead with the transmission: when US yields rise, emerging and Muslim-majority borrowers (Pakistan, Egypt, Nigeria) refinance dearer and cut spending on their own people to pay creditors. Give the IMF's numbers on debt-service share of revenue where the report has them, and name the series: the US 10-year Treasury yield.

stories.label: Shell to sell Nigeria's domestic gas business to Vaaris Energy
stories.summary: Shell has agreed to sell all of Shell Nigeria Gas, which pipes gas to factories and power users at home, to Vaaris Energy. Lead with what changes hands and the price if disclosed; the mechanism is the long Western exit from Nigerian onshore assets (Shell's 2025 onshore sale to Renaissance, Exxon, Eni) while the majors keep the deepwater and export LNG. Who inherits the pipelines, the liabilities and the Niger Delta communities, and whether domestic supply gets cheaper or less reliable.

stories.label: OpenAI employee arrested for planting recording device at office
stories.summary: The FBI arrested Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi national working as an OpenAI engineer, and charged him over a recording device found behind a television in an OpenAI conference room in San Francisco. Lead with what was found and the charge, stated as allegations. The structural point: frontier labs are now treated as national-security targets, and the reader should know what the complaint says about motive or any foreign link, and what it does not; do not imply state direction the charging papers do not allege.

stories.label: Claude写代码太快，Anthropic先扛不住了：连Git都要重做
stories.summary: Anthropic has replaced Git in its monorepo with Scion, a server-side source-control system built by seven people in five months, because AI agents now merge over 30,000 changes a day, up twelvefold from about 2,500 in May. Lead with the load: about 25 million CI checkouts a day and an estimated 600PB of Git traffic, a main-branch history near 100GB. The mechanism for developers: always-online clients, server-side commits and merges, changesets in a write-ahead log on Spanner, virtualised sparse checkouts, a footprint 1/200 of the Git mirrors. The point: tools built for human-paced coding break first when agents write the code. Anthropic says it will not release Scion as a product.

stories.label: Gemini 4 Argon全球上线，API限时五折，谷歌要杀回第一梯队！
stories.summary: Google has opened Gemini 4 Argon, its flagship model announced 1 October, to developers and businesses worldwide at a launch price cut by half: $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output, with cached input 95% off, until 30 November. Lead with the price: it is a bid to win agent workloads back from OpenAI and Anthropic, and the reader should see how it compares per token. Report the benchmark claims (first on the Vals Index) as Google's own, and the demos (CAD from a sketch, 1,000 self-checking iterations) as demos.

stories.label: Isle of Wight fossil sheds light on enigmatic meat-eating dinosaurs
stories.summary: Researchers have named Invictibellatrix amberina, an early megaraptoran found on the Isle of Wight, the first of this Cretaceous lineage of carnivores known from Europe; until now they were known mostly from South America, Australia and Asia. Lead with where it was found and why that is surprising; the mechanism is biogeography: an early European member bears on where megaraptorans arose and how they spread before the continents parted. Name the journal and the skull features the paper adds.

stories.label: PTI protest in Bara turns violent as demonstrators clash with police
stories.summary: New since this morning's piece on the arrests of PTI workers and legislators in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (one clause): the crackdown has met resistance on the street. A PTI protest in Bara tehsil, Khyber district, turned violent on Tuesday; Dawn reports police firing live rounds and tear gas, protesters manhandling officers, and government buildings set on fire. Lead with the live fire and the burned buildings, and any casualties the page confirms (it cites Hayatabad Medical Complex). Mechanism: say what the protest was called against, who ordered the police response, and why Bara, an Afridi tribal area merged into the province only in 2018, is where a party dispute turns into a confrontation with the state. Say what Dawn could verify and what it could not, and give the provincial and federal governments' and PTI's accounts as their own. Single source, the Pakistani paper of record. Write your own headline. Dateline Bara.

stories.label: State security prosecution renews detention of 6 Matsda2sh journalists for 15 days
stories.summary: Egypt's Supreme State Security Prosecution renewed for 15 days the detention of six journalists from the fact-checking platform Matsda2sh (Mohamed Ashraf Abu Emaira, Abdallah Kadry, Islam Barakat, Mohamed Adel, Mohamed Mahmoud and Omar Helal) in Case 8083/2026, their lawyers say. Lead with six fact-checkers held and the renewal. Mechanism: pretrial detention in Egypt is renewed in 15-day blocks by the same prosecution that brings the case, so a person can be held for months or years without trial; say what the six are accused of, when they were arrested, and what the platform published. Set it beside the draft law reported this afternoon that would ban jailing journalists in publishing cases (one clause): the constitution already forbids it, and this is the practice the bill is aimed at. Give the prosecution's position, or that it has given none. Mada Masr is the Egyptian outlet and is itself blocked in Egypt. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Cairo.

stories.label: Destruction of Gaza Court System Strips Women of Their Rights
stories.summary: With Gaza's courts destroyed, Palestinian women cannot enforce rights to inheritance, divorce, alimony and property, Drop Site reports. Lead with the women the report names and what each cannot obtain. Mechanism: family law in Gaza runs through sharia courts whose buildings, archives and judges the war destroyed or scattered, so a widow cannot prove a marriage or a death, register an inheritance or collect maintenance; say how many courts functioned before and how many do now, what happened to the records, and what stand-ins (informal committees, clan mediation) decide in their place and in whose favour. The accountability point: the destruction of a judiciary has a named author, and its cost falls on those with the least power inside the society; give the Israeli authorities' and Gaza authorities' replies if the page has them. Distinct from this morning's piece on families sleeping in damaged buildings; do not retell it. Drop Site uses the word genocide; attribute characterisations and write the facts. No regional outlet in the feed carries it. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Gaza City, or as the report places it.

stories.label: Trump says he does not believe China and Russia help Iran, contradicting US intelligence
stories.summary: President Trump said on Truth Social that he does not believe China and Russia are helping Iran 'at all', while US intelligence reports in recent months have found that both directly support Tehran. Lead with the contradiction: the commander of a war publicly rejecting his own agencies' finding about who is supplying the other side. Mechanism: say what the intelligence reports found (what kind of support, as the pages give it), what prompted the post, and what follows from the president's position: no sanctions or pressure on Beijing and Moscow over Iran, at a moment when the US is enforcing a blockade in the Strait of Hormuz and negotiating with both powers on other files. Give Beijing's, Moscow's and Tehran's statements if a page has them. One clause on today's Hormuz attacks at most; do not retell them. Write from Al-Monitor (a Reuters report); the Middle East Eye link is a live-blog entry carrying the same text. State the intelligence findings as reported, not as established. Write your own headline. Dateline Washington. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: UK ambassador summoned to Iran's foreign ministry
stories.summary: New since Monday's piece on London blaming Iran's Revolutionary Guards for the incident at RAF Fairford, the airbase used by US forces (one clause): Tehran has answered formally. Iran's foreign ministry summoned the British ambassador, Hugo Shorter, on Tuesday to protest what it calls baseless allegations, the Iranian state news agency Mehr reports; assistant foreign minister Alireza Yousefi delivered the protest. Lead with the summons and what Iran told the ambassador. Mechanism: say what Britain alleged and on what published evidence, what Iran denies, and what each side can do next (expulsions, proscription of the Guards, which London has long debated), with Britain hosting US aircraft used in the war on Iran. Mehr is Iranian state media and the only source: attribute every claim to it and to the ministry, state nothing as fact beyond the summons itself, and do not carry Tehran's adjectives. No independent or British outlet in the feed carries it. Write your own headline. Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: After flood disasters, Nepal needs clear numbers on aid and a reconstruction plan
stories.summary: Nepal's flood-hit communities are waiting on rebuilding while nobody can say how much aid has arrived or where it went, Global Voices reports. Lead with the people still without homes and the missing figures, not the floods themselves. Mechanism: say what was destroyed (homes, roads, bridges, livelihoods, with the counts the page gives), how much relief was pledged and by whom, which body is responsible for accounting for it, and why there is no reconstruction plan: who decides between federal, provincial and local government. The accountability point: after a disaster the money is the story, and Nepal's 2015 earthquake reconstruction is the precedent readers should be given in a clause if the page gives it. This is a politics story about aid and the state, not a weather or science story. The headline is the outlet's argument: write the reported facts, attribute judgments to the people quoted, and write your own neutral headline. Single source. Dateline as the report places it (Kathmandu or the affected district).

stories.label: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs2.71 per litre, high-speed diesel rate by Re0.03
stories.summary: Pakistan cut petrol by Rs2.71 to Rs392.66 a litre and diesel by three paisa to Rs396.82, while the state keeps taking Rs114 on every litre in taxes and levies. Lead with the tax, not the cut: more than a quarter of what a Pakistani pays at the pump is the government's share, and the fortnightly revision moved the price by under 1%. Mechanism: say how the price is built (import cost tracking the price of Brent crude and the rupee, then the petroleum levy, climate levy and margins, as the page breaks them down), why the levy is where it is (IMF programme revenue targets), and why diesel, the fuel of freight and farm tractors, barely moved. Name the series plainly: the price of Brent crude, with the Strait of Hormuz closure behind it. Who it lands on: households and transporters in a country the UNDP index reported this morning (one clause) as poorer than its neighbours. Give the minister's statement as the page has it. Single source, Dawn. Write your own headline. Dateline Islamabad.

stories.label: Parks Tau brought the transformation fight to the automotive industry
stories.summary: South Africa's trade minister, Parks Tau, used a keynote to the motor industry to demand more Black ownership and more locally made parts from the foreign carmakers that assemble there. Lead with what he asked for and of whom: the targets, the deadline and the incentives at stake, as the page gives them. Mechanism: the plants belong to Toyota, VW, BMW, Mercedes, Ford and others and exist because of a state incentive scheme, so the government's lever is the subsidy; the carmakers' lever is that they can leave, with US tariffs, cheap Chinese imports and the shift to plug-in vehicles already squeezing exports. Say how much local content the industry has against its target and what the manufacturers answered. Who it lands on: more than 100,000 autoworkers and the Black-owned suppliers the policy is meant to create. The page is labelled analysis: write the announcements and figures as news and attribute judgments to Daily Maverick. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline as the report places the speech.

stories.label: 一只18A“超购王”的停摆：停牌半年、调出港股通，中慧生物年内第三位董事辞任
stories.summary: A Chinese biotech that was among the most oversubscribed listings under Hong Kong's Chapter 18A, the rule that lets drug developers with no revenue go public, has been suspended from trading for half a year, removed from the Stock Connect scheme that lets mainland investors buy it, and has just lost its third director this year, TMTPost, a mainland Chinese business outlet, reports. Lead with the retail investors locked in: the shares cannot be sold, the annual report has not been filed, and an independent forensic investigation is under way. Mechanism: say what 18A allows and why it drew a rush of subscriptions, what triggered the suspension (the auditor, the unfiled accounts, what the forensic inquiry is examining), what removal from Stock Connect does to mainland holders, and what the exchange's delisting clock is. The structural point: Hong Kong reopened its IPO market on pre-revenue biotech, and this is what a failure in that regime looks like. In Chinese; translate the company name (Zhonghui Biotech, 中慧生物), figures and dates exactly, attribute to TMTPost, state allegations as allegations. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Hong Kong.

stories.label: Walmart to offer 250-plus free medications, including GLP-1s, to employees
stories.summary: Walmart, the largest private employer in the United States, will give employees more than 250 medications at no cost, including GLP-1 obesity and diabetes drugs, insulin and inhalers. Lead with the scale: how many workers are covered and from when, and that the list includes drugs that cost hundreds of dollars a month. Mechanism: Walmart insures its own workforce and runs its own pharmacies, so it buys the drugs at its own cost and pays its own claims; say who qualifies (which health plans, full-time or part-time), what the company expects to save or spend, and what it means for the drugmakers and for other employers that have been dropping GLP-1 coverage as too expensive. Who it lands on: low-wage workers in a country where a job decides whether insulin is affordable. Walmart's shares are up 7.6% in a week: say so only if the page ties the move to a cause, and do not attribute it to this plan yourself. Reuters brief, single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Bentonville. US dateline (4 of 3: see summary).

stories.label: Can GLP-1s heal the brain? Obesity drugs get a makeover for addiction and depression
stories.summary: Drug companies are now developing GLP-1-related compounds, the class behind the obesity drugs, to treat addiction, schizophrenia, depression and other brain disorders, building on years of academic work, Nature reports. Lead with the shift: a gut-hormone drug being re-engineered for the brain, with new money behind it. Mechanism for a technical reader: say where GLP-1 receptors sit in the brain and what they do to reward and craving, what the evidence is so far and of what kind (observational data from people taking the drugs for weight, animal studies, which randomised trials have reported and what they found), why existing drugs reach the brain poorly and how the new compounds differ, and which companies and trials the piece names. Say what is not shown: the trials that failed or were null, and the psychiatric side-effect questions. This is Nature's news reporting, not a paper: attribute to Nature and the researchers it quotes, and state no effect as established that the trials have not established. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline as the report places it.

stories.label: Character.ai's Bankruptcy Documents Show the Economics of AI Don't Work
stories.summary: Character.ai's bankruptcy filings show a consumer AI company that degraded its product to cut costs and raise revenue and was still burning cash, 404 Media reports. Lead with the numbers in the court documents: revenue, what it cost to run the models, the losses, the debts and to whom. Mechanism for a technical reader: every message a user sends costs compute, so usage that would be profit for a normal app is cost here; say what the company did to close the gap (ads, paywalls, cheaper models, limits) and why the filings say it was not enough, who the creditors are (cloud providers, investors), and what happens to users' conversations and to the lawsuits over harm to minors in a bankruptcy. The structural point: one of the most-used chatbot products could not cover inference with subscriptions, which is a data point about the whole sector. The feed entry is a one-line teaser: read the page first and write only what the filings, as 404 Media reports them, support; the headline's generalisation is the outlet's. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline as the filing's court. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: ESA targets Anbernic emulation handhelds as "superfake" piracy enablers
stories.summary: The Entertainment Software Association, the US video-game industry's trade group (the feed's tags confuse it with the European Space Agency; it is not), has asked the US Trade Representative to act against Anbernic, a Chinese maker of handheld Android consoles built for retro emulation. Lead with the request and its target: a hardware maker, not a site hosting pirated games. Mechanism for a technical reader: say what the ESA asked for (listing on the USTR's notorious-markets review, as the page gives it) and what that listing does and does not do legally, what 'superfake' means in the filing, and where the legal line sits: emulators are lawful in the US, pre-loaded copyrighted ROMs are not, and the filing argues the devices ship with or steer buyers to the latter. Say what Anbernic sells and answers. The structural point: a trade lobby using trade policy against a foreign device maker where copyright suits have not reached, with implications for every open handheld. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Washington. US dateline (3 of 3).

stories.label: 在AI时代“改变世界”，买电、买算力，还是造底座？
stories.summary: Envision, the Chinese wind-turbine and battery group, says it has built at Ulanqab in Inner Mongolia what it calls the world's largest single AI computing block: a 120,000-square-metre data centre fed more than 80% by its own wind farms over a dedicated line, and it plans 5 GW of such desert sites by 2030 under a programme named Mission Gobi, Zhidx, a mainland Chinese tech outlet, reports. Lead with the design choice: put the computing where the wind and sun are, and plan generation, storage and servers as one system off the public grid. Mechanism for a technical reader: say why that is hard (intermittent supply against a load that runs around the clock, with no grid behind it), and what Envision says it uses: forecasting and dispatch models, battery storage, an 800-volt direct-current feed through solid-state transformers that removes conversion steps, liquid cooling, and domestic chips. The structural point is the view from inside China's industry: the binding constraint on AI has moved from chips to electricity, substations take 12 to 18 months and customers want capacity in six, and a turbine maker is entering the data-centre business from the power side. The piece is admiring and reads close to company material: state every figure and every superlative as Envision's claim, leave out the Fortune list, and say what is not independently shown (how the site runs when the wind drops, actual utilisation, cost per unit of compute). In Chinese; translate names and specifications exactly. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Ulanqab.

stories.label: Iran hits supertanker in Strait of Hormuz -- IRGC
stories.summary: New since Monday night's piece on the third tanker hit in two days (one clause): six commercial vessels were hit in the Strait of Hormuz in a single day, the heaviest spate of the war, after a US fighter jet disabled an Iran-linked tanker that the US military accused of trying to run its naval blockade (Al-Monitor). Lead with six ships in a day and the US strike that preceded them. The mechanism: two blockades overlap in one channel, the US firing on ships it says serve Iran and the Revolutionary Guards hitting ships they call 'offending', so each enforcement action is answered on merchant hulls; say which ships were hit, their flags, cargo and crews, what CENTCOM and the IRGC each claim, and what is independently confirmed. Name the series plainly: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and the price of Brent crude. Who it lands on: the crews, mostly South and Southeast Asian seafarers, and fuel importers in Asia. Write from Al-Monitor; TASS is Russian state media and Mehr is Iranian state media, used only for the Guards' own statement, attributed. Write your own headline. Dateline as Al-Monitor places the events (the strait), not Washington.

stories.label: Police detain leaders of India's 'cockroach' movement at New Delhi protest
stories.summary: New since Monday's piece on the Delhi march over the voter-roll revision (one clause): the state has moved against the organisers. Delhi police detained leaders of the youth-led 'cockroach' movement after they jumped barricades into Jantar Mantar, the capital's customary protest ground, which the authorities have closed, and filed a criminal case against named leaders (India.com names Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das). Lead with the detentions and the closed protest site. The mechanism: the movement demands the chief election commissioner resign over revisions of the voter lists that leave millions, many of them poor and Muslim, having to prove their right to vote; say what the revision requires of a voter, how many names are at stake as the pages give it, what charges the FIR carries, and why shutting the one sanctioned protest ground turns a march into an offence. Give the Election Commission's and the police's replies. New Lines Magazine has ground reportage on the roll revision the writer may read for the mechanism (https://newlinesmag.com/reportage/in-india-citizens-brace-for-a-democratic-unraveling/). Write your own headline. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: EU opens two more Ukraine accession clusters as Hungary lifts veto
stories.summary: EU governments have agreed to open two more accession clusters with Ukraine after Hungary dropped its veto, following an agreement on the rights of Ukraine's ethnic Hungarian minority; Zelenskyy and Hungary's prime minister Péter Magyar may meet in Brussels this week. Lead with the veto lifted and what it unblocks. The mechanism: accession moves by unanimity, so one capital held 40 million people's candidacy for years over the language and schooling rights of a minority of some tens of thousands in Transcarpathia; say which clusters open and which remain shut, what Kyiv conceded on minority rights (the feed tags the Verkhovna Rada and the Ukrainian language law), and what changed in Budapest with the new government. The structural point: opening clusters is not membership, and every later step needs all 27 again. Distinct from this morning's piece on the energy ceasefire; do not retell it. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Brussels.

stories.label: Photos: French protests over school conditions swell
stories.summary: Some 161,500 people marched across France on Tuesday, by the Interior Ministry's count, in support of high school students protesting the state of their schools, a movement Al Jazeera says is posing a major challenge to President Macron as his term winds down. Lead with the turnout and who joined the pupils (parents, teachers, unions, as the page gives it), with the organisers' own figure beside the ministry's. The mechanism: say what the students are protesting in concrete terms (the buildings, staffing, which schools and where; the feed tags Saint-Denis, the poorest department of mainland France), who pays for school buildings in France (regions and departments, not the state) and why that leaves the poorest districts with the worst ones, and what the government has offered. The page is a photo gallery with a text introduction: write only what its text supports. Unrelated to this afternoon's piece on the Aubagne school shooting; do not link them. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Paris.

stories.label: Политблогер Сыргак Кенжебаев задержан за границей и доставлен в Кыргызстан
stories.summary: Kyrgyzstan's interior ministry says Syrgak Kenzhebaev, a political blogger who runs the YouTube channel 'Er-Syrgak' and had spent the past two months criticising the government, was detained abroad and brought back to Kyrgyzstan, Kloop reports. Lead with that: a critic seized outside the country and delivered home. The mechanism: say in which country he was held and by whom, under what legal procedure if any (extradition, deportation, or none stated), what he is charged with, and what his channel had been saying; set it beside the pattern Kloop documents, that critics who leave are no longer out of reach. Kloop reports the same day that the author of the tax service's own investigation into the Tashiev family and Kyrgyzneftegaz says he is being persecuted (https://kloop.kg/blog/2026/10/13/po-puti-temirova-avtor-rassledovaniya-nalogovoj-o-klane-tashievyh-soobshhil-o-presledovanii/): one or two sentences from that page if it loads, as a second case, not a second story. Give the ministry's account as its own. In Russian; translate names and charges exactly and attribute to Kloop, an independent Kyrgyz outlet that is itself blocked in the country. The feed entry is a teaser: read the page first and write only what it supports. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Bishkek.

stories.label: Argentina lodges legal claim against UK's Falklands oil exploration
stories.summary: Argentina has lodged a legal claim against oil exploration off the Falkland Islands (Malvinas), where the Sea Lion field, about 130 miles (209 km) from the islands, is estimated to hold 1.7 billion barrels; the islands' government extended exploration licences last month, and a British minister told the Commons 'we will do whatever it takes to support them'. Lead with the claim and the forum (the feed tags the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea and the continental shelf): what Buenos Aires asks the tribunal to order, and against whom. The mechanism: a sovereignty dispute that a war did not settle is being reopened as a law-of-the-sea case over who may license the seabed, at a moment when oil above $100 makes a marginal South Atlantic field worth drilling; say who operates Sea Lion, when production is planned, and whether the UK accepts the tribunal's jurisdiction. Name the series plainly: the price of Brent crude, in one sentence. Use both names for the islands once, then follow the BBC. Give Argentina's own statement as the page has it; no Argentine outlet in the feed carries it. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Buenos Aires.

stories.label: Hackers Turn French Supermarket Refrigerators Into Furnaces
stories.summary: New since Monday's piece on fridges defrosted in some 200 French supermarkets (one clause): the attack is larger and more dangerous than first reported, and it is now a national criminal investigation. OCCRP reports that hundreds of stores were hit overnight on 11 to 12 October, that the hijacked refrigeration systems were driven into intense defrost cycles that spoiled vast quantities of food and started fires, and that prosecutors have opened a nationwide case. Lead with the fires and the investigation, not the spoiled food. The mechanism for a technical reader: say how one intrusion reached hundreds of sites (a shared remote-management or building-control platform for commercial refrigeration, as the pages give it), which chains were hit (the feed tags Intermarché and E.Leclerc), who is suspected and on what evidence, and why Al Jazeera says supermarkets have become a target: thin margins, outsourced operational technology, and equipment never designed to face the internet. Who it lands on: shoppers and store staff, and insurers pricing a cyberattack that causes physical fire. State attribution of the attack as the investigators' or as unknown. Write your own headline. Dateline Paris.

stories.label: Natural gas price in Europe above $1,000 per 1,000 cubic meters
stories.summary: European natural gas futures on the Dutch TTF hub have crossed $1,000 per thousand cubic metres, their highest since 2022, with storage at record lows for the time of year before winter, according to ICE exchange data as relayed by the Russian state news agency TASS. Lead with the level and the storage figure, attributed. The mechanism: Europe replaced Russian pipeline gas with liquefied gas bought on the world market, a large share of it from Qatar through the Strait of Hormuz, which is shut, so it enters winter with tanks it could not fill and bids against Asia for every remaining cargo; give the storage percentage against the usual level and the price in euros per megawatt-hour as the page has them. Name the series plainly: the price of natural gas and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Who it lands on: European households and industry, and poorer importers such as Pakistan and Bangladesh who are outbid for the same cargoes. TASS is Russian state media and the only source: attribute every figure to ICE as TASS reports it, and do not carry Moscow's framing of Europe's choices. Write your own headline. Dateline Amsterdam (TTF), not Moscow.

stories.label: MegaETH-powered MNX goes live with pre-IPO futures for OpenAI, Anthropic and DeepSeek
stories.summary: A new crypto exchange, MNX, has begun offering futures on the valuations of private AI companies (OpenAI, Anthropic and DeepSeek) with up to three times leverage, to anyone except US customers. Lead with what is actually being traded: not shares, but a bet on a price that no public market sets. The mechanism for a technical reader: say how the contract is priced when the underlying company has no listed stock (which reference the exchange uses: funding rounds, secondary sales, an oracle), who takes the other side, how it settles, where the exchange is registered, and why US customers are excluded (securities law). The structural point: the largest AI firms have stayed private, so ordinary investors cannot buy them, and offshore venues are now selling synthetic exposure with leverage and none of the disclosure a listing would require; say what the companies themselves have said about such products, if the page does. CoinDesk is a trade outlet: no price commentary, and state the exchange's claims as claims. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline as the report places the exchange.

stories.label: Variations in the human vocal tract could have influenced language diversity
stories.summary: Small anatomical differences in the human vocal tract may be one source of the differences between the world's languages, according to a study in PLOS Biology by Steven Moran, Tiena Danner and colleagues at the University of Neuchâtel. Lead with the claim in plain terms: the shape of the mouth and throat, which varies between populations, may nudge which sounds a language keeps. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what the team measured (which anatomical features, in how many people or populations, by what imaging or modelling), which sounds they link to which anatomy, how large the effect is, and how they separate anatomy from shared ancestry and contact between languages. Say what the authors do not claim: that anatomy determines language, or that any group's speech is constrained. Give an outside linguist's view if the page has one. It is a university press summary carried by Phys.org: attribute to the study and name the journal. The feed entry is a teaser: read the page first. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Neuchâtel.

stories.label: This bacterium cleans up toxic textile wastewater
stories.summary: A bacterium isolated from textile effluent itself can break down a synthetic azo dye, the class of dyes that gives cloth its vivid colours and resists ordinary wastewater treatment, Nature India reports. Lead with where the organism was found and what it does. The mechanism for a technical reader: name the species and the dye, say how fast and how completely it degrades it and under what conditions (concentration, temperature, pH, with or without oxygen), which enzymes do the work, and whether the breakdown products are themselves toxic, since azo dyes can split into carcinogenic amines. Say at what scale it has been shown (flask, reactor) and what stands between that and a dye works. Who it lands on: the rivers and the people downstream of the textile clusters of India and Bangladesh, where much of the world's clothing is dyed. Name the researchers, their institution and the journal the paper is in. It is Nature India's research highlight, not a Nature paper: attribute accordingly. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline as the report places the lead institution.

stories.label: They war-gamed dimming the Sun. It went even worse than you think.
stories.summary: A series of war games that began in London last September put climate researchers, among them Colleen Golja, in rooms with players acting as governments to test whether the world could prevent an uncontrolled deployment of solar geoengineering, and the exercises went badly: science and reason, Golja found, did not get a seat at the table. Lead with what the games were for and how they ended. The mechanism: say who ran them and who played, what scenario they started from (a state or a company starting to spray reflective particles on its own), what the players did, and why restraint failed: the technology is cheap enough for one actor, its effects cross every border, and no treaty or body has authority over it. Say what the organisers conclude should be built before anyone deploys, and what real-world programmes the piece cites (the feed tags SpaceX). Who it lands on: countries whose monsoons and harvests would shift under a decision taken elsewhere. It is a long report, republished from Wired: write the findings of the exercises as news, attribute judgments to the participants, and leave the scene-setting. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline London.

stories.label: Anthropic conjures another threat that doesn't exist yet to stoke fears of AI apocalypse
stories.summary: Anthropic published research on Monday saying AI models could within months be able to copy themselves across vulnerable internet-connected home devices as a self-replicating worm, and The Register answers that the lab has again described a threat that does not yet exist, noting that fear sells AI products. Lead with the claim and the dispute together. The mechanism for a technical reader: say exactly what Anthropic tested (which models, in what environment, against which devices; the feed tags Android TV boxes), what the models did and failed to do, what 'self-replicate' means for a model whose weights are tens of gigabytes on hardware with a few gigabytes of memory, and what assumption turns a lab result into 'within months'. Then The Register's objections in its own terms, and Al Jazeera's account for the plain summary. The structural point: the companies that build the models are also the main source of evidence about their dangers, and a warning is both a safety disclosure and marketing; the insecure consumer devices are real either way. The feed's title is The Register's opinionated headline: write a neutral one. State Anthropic's findings as its claims and the criticism as The Register's. Dateline San Francisco. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Tesla's 'Security Protocols' Stopped DHS From Installing a Tracking Device
stories.summary: A federal warrant application shows that agents of the US Department of Homeland Security could not attach a tracking device to a suspected drug trafficker's Tesla because of the car's 'security protocols', 404 Media reports. Lead with the document and what it admits. The mechanism for a technical reader: say which feature stopped them, as the filing describes it (Sentry Mode's cameras recording and alerting the owner when someone approaches the car, or another protocol), what the agents asked the court for instead (location data from Tesla itself, a different warrant), and whether Tesla complied. The structural point cuts both ways: a car that watches its surroundings defeats a covert tracker, and the same car reports its location to its maker, so the surveillance moves from a device under the bumper to a request served on a company; say what the filing shows about how often that route is used. Attribute everything to the court record as 404 Media reports it; the suspect is accused, not convicted, and need not be named. The feed entry is short: read the page first. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline as the filing's court district. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: China’s five-ton-payload robot debuts at Shanghai’s CIIF, but real-world performance is what counts
stories.summary: An industrial robot rated to carry more than five tons went on show at the China International Industry Fair, which opened in Shanghai on Monday, and TechNode, a China-based tech outlet, asks the question the exhibit does not answer: whether it works on a factory floor. Lead with the machine and its maker, then the caveat. The mechanism for a technical reader: say why payload is the hard number (robots have competed on precision, speed and repeatability, and at five tons the arm's own deflection, the reducers and the control of inertia become the problem), what the robot is meant to handle (large castings, ship, rail or wind-turbine components), which parts are domestic and which imported, and how it compares with the heaviest arms from Fanuc, KUKA or ABB, as the piece gives it. The structural point is the view from inside China's industry: the country installs more robots than the rest of the world combined, and its makers are moving from the cheap end of the market into the heavy, high-margin end that Japanese and European firms held; say what TechNode says still has to be proved (uptime, accuracy under load, customers). State the maker's figures as its claims and TechNode's judgments as its own. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Shanghai.

stories.label: School shooting horror as head and teacher 'attacked by student with shotgun'
stories.summary: France's anti-terror prosecutor has taken over the case of a 14-year-old who shot and wounded a headmaster and a teacher at a school in Aubagne, near Marseille, because he may have belonged to the 'True Crime Community', an online network that glorifies mass killers. Lead with the takeover and why it is unusual: there is no ideology in the usual sense, and the state is treating a fandom of school shooters as terrorism. The mechanism: say what the network is and where it lives online, what investigators found linking the boy to it, how he got a shotgun in a country with tight gun law, and what charges a 14-year-old can face. Give the victims' condition and the government's response (platform regulation, school security) as the pages have them. The feed's title is tabloid: write from France 24, Al Jazeera and Dawn, state the link to the network as the prosecutor's suspicion, do not name the minor, and write your own headline. Dateline Aubagne.

stories.label: Tusk: Two Suspected Saboteurs Arrested in Germany
stories.summary: German police, acting on a Polish request, have arrested two Turkish citizens suspected of setting fire to a Starlink ground station in Poland, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said, and Warsaw accuses Russian intelligence of ordering it; a third person has since been detained in Germany (Reuters via Yahoo). Lead with the target and the arrests: satellite-internet infrastructure that Ukraine's army depends on, attacked on NATO soil. The mechanism: the pattern Poland describes is sabotage by hire, in which third-country nationals are recruited online and paid per job, so the people caught are disposable and the link to Moscow rests on intelligence, not on a court finding; say what evidence Warsaw has made public, what the station does and how badly it was damaged, and what Germany's prosecutors have charged. State the Russian link as Poland's accusation and give Moscow's reply and Ankara's, if a page has them. One clause on the earlier arrest over a plot against Tusk. Al Jazeera is in the cluster. Dateline Warsaw.

stories.label: From journalists’ pursuit to protection? Bid to ban jail sentences for publishing gets boost from syndicate, MPs
stories.summary: Egypt's constitution already forbids jailing journalists for what they publish, and they are jailed anyway; a draft law to close that gap has now won the backing of the Journalists Syndicate and a group of MPs, who met at the syndicate's Cairo headquarters to agree practical steps. Lead with the contradiction and the draft: what it would ban (pretrial detention and custodial sentences in publishing cases), who drafted it and when, and where it stands in parliament. The mechanism: say which laws prosecutors use to get round the constitutional protection (the penal code, the cybercrime and terrorism laws, 'spreading false news'), how many journalists are held, as the page gives it, and why a constitutional article with no implementing law protects no one. Give the government's position, or that it has given none. Mada Masr is the Egyptian outlet and is itself blocked in Egypt; say so in a clause. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Cairo.

stories.label: Anhörung zur Geheimdienstreform: „Ich habe noch nie eine Vorschrift gesehen, die so offensichtlich verfassungswidrig ist“
stories.summary: Experts called before the Bundestag told MPs that Germany's planned reform of its intelligence services is unconstitutional; one said he had 'never seen a provision so obviously unconstitutional'. Lead with that verdict and who gave it. The mechanism: say what the bill gives the BND and the domestic services (which new powers, over whose communications), and the three objections the experts raised: it enables mass surveillance, it dissolves the separation of police and intelligence services that Germany wrote into its post-1945 order because of the Gestapo, and its oversight is too weak. Say which earlier Constitutional Court rulings the bill has to satisfy, what the government's own witnesses answered, and what happens next in committee. In German; translate names, titles and quotations exactly and attribute to netzpolitik.org and the experts it quotes. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Berlin.

stories.label: India delays digital payments fee rollout amid retailer pushback
stories.summary: India has put off its plan to charge merchants a fee on UPI, the free instant-payments network that carries most of the country's digital transactions, after shopkeepers across the country pushed back. Lead with the delay: what the National Payments Corporation of India had planned (the rate, which merchants, from when), the new date if there is one, and that it comes just before Diwali. The mechanism: UPI is free by government policy, so the apps that run on it, dominated by Google Pay and PhonePe, earn almost nothing from payments, and the state has covered the cost with a subsidy; the fee was meant to make the business pay for itself, and small retailers on thin margins said they would pass it on or go back to cash. Who holds power: a state-backed utility, two foreign-owned apps and millions of kirana shops. Give the volumes and the subsidy figures as the page has them. UPI is the model other Global South countries are copying, so who pays for it matters beyond India. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline as the report places it (Mumbai for NPCI, or New Delhi).

stories.label: Seven OPEC+ countries scale up oil production by 977,000 bpd in September
stories.summary: Seven OPEC+ countries that had been holding back output pumped 26.123 million barrels a day in September, 977,000 more than in August, with Saudi Arabia adding the most, according to OPEC's monthly report as relayed by the Russian state news agency TASS. Lead with the increase and its odd timing: nearly a million barrels a day more from producers whose main export route, the Strait of Hormuz, is shut. The mechanism: say where the extra barrels go (Saudi Arabia's east-west pipeline to the Red Sea, storage, Kazakh and Iraqi routes that avoid the Gulf, as the page gives it), which of the seven raised output and which could not, how the totals compare with each country's quota, and why producing more does not mean delivering more while shipping and insurance take a third of a cargo's value (this morning's piece, one clause). Name the series plainly: the price of Brent crude and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Who it lands on: fuel importers in Asia and Africa waiting on cargoes. TASS is Russian state media and the only source: attribute every figure to OPEC's report as TASS reports it, and do not carry Moscow's framing. No Saudi, Iraqi or Kazakh outlet in the feed carries it. Write your own headline. Dateline Vienna.

stories.label: Exclusive: Giraffe Bio aims its bespoke biomolecules at the looming copper shortage
stories.summary: The world may be a quarter short of the copper it needs by 2040, as AI data centres and electrification pull on a metal whose supply grows mostly by opening new mines, which takes a decade or more and a good deal of luck. Lead with that gap and the alternative this startup is selling: engineered biomolecules that pull more copper out of ore and waste rock at mines already running. The mechanism for a technical reader: say how the chemistry works against conventional acid leaching and microbial bioleaching, on what grade of ore, what recovery the company claims and at what scale it has been shown (lab, pilot, a named mine), who funds it and how much it raised. The structural point: the copper is in Chile, Peru, the DRC, Zambia and Indonesia, and a method that raises yield from existing pits changes who needs new concessions, and what is left in the tailings. Name the series plainly: the price of copper. The 2040 shortfall is a forecast: attribute it. Company claims are claims; no valuation talk. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline as the report places the company.

stories.label: Honey bee stingers are double-piston venom pumps
stories.summary: A honey bee's stinger keeps pumping venom into its victim after the bee has torn itself away and flown off, and scientists have now worked out how: the detached stinger is a self-contained double-piston pump. Lead with the finding in plain mechanical terms. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what the two pistons are anatomically (the barbed lancets sliding on the stylet), what drives them once the bee is gone (the muscles and nerve ganglion that tear away with the sting), how the valves keep venom moving one way, how long it pumps and how much it delivers, and how the team saw it (high-speed imaging, micro-CT, a physical or computational model). Name the researchers, their institution and the journal. Why it matters beyond bees: say what the authors propose it could inform (microneedles, drug-delivery pumps) only if the page says so, and the practical point about removing a sting quickly. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline as the report places the lead institution.

stories.label: Inundated AI conferences impose submissions caps
stories.summary: The leading conferences and journals in artificial intelligence are capping how many papers one researcher may submit, because they can no longer review what arrives; ICLR 2027 is among them, Nature reports. Lead with the cap: the number, who it binds (per author, per first author), and how many submissions the conference received against earlier years. The mechanism: in machine learning the conference paper is the unit of a career, hiring and visas follow paper counts, and language models now help write papers and reviews alike, so submissions grow faster than the pool of qualified reviewers; say what the organisers found (authors on dozens of papers, review quality, machine-written reviews) and which other venues, the Association for Computational Linguistics among them, have done the same. Who it lands on: students and researchers in large labs, including in China and India, whose names go on many papers, and what critics say a cap does to them. This is Nature's news reporting, not a paper: attribute to Nature and the organisers it quotes. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline as the report places it.

stories.label: Gesichtersuchmaschine PimEyes: Ein Verbot, das niemand durchsetzt
stories.summary: For more than a year EU law has banned building face-recognition databases by scraping images from the internet, and PimEyes, a search engine that finds a stranger's photos across the web from one picture of their face, is still operating; netzpolitik.org reports that Germany's designated regulator, the Federal Network Agency, will not say what it is doing and that the federal government is manoeuvring around the ban. Lead with the gap between the prohibition and the product. The mechanism for a technical reader: say which provision bans it (the AI Act's prohibition on untargeted scraping of facial images, in force since February 2025), what PimEyes does and where the company is registered, why enforcement falls between national authorities, what penalties the law allows and that none has been imposed, and what the agency, the government and PimEyes answered. The structural point: a ban is only as real as the authority assigned to enforce it, and the people it protects, stalking victims and protesters among them, cannot enforce it themselves. In German; translate exactly and attribute findings to netzpolitik.org. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Berlin.

stories.label: Microsoft plans multi-gigawatt rollout of next-gen Azure Maia AI accelerator racks
stories.summary: Microsoft has shown the next generation of its own Azure Maia AI chips and says it will deploy them by the gigawatt, in racks designed as one system for what it calls agentic inference. Lead with the scale, counted in power not in chips, and what it replaces: capacity Microsoft would otherwise buy from Nvidia. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what the new Maia is (process node and foundry, memory, networking, cooling, how it compares with the Maia 200 announced earlier this year, as The Register gives it), why inference for agents favours a cheaper custom part over a general-purpose GPU, and which workloads and customers (OpenAI, Copilot) will run on it. The structural point: every large cloud now designs its own accelerator, so Nvidia's biggest customers are becoming its competitors, and the binding constraint moves from chips to electricity; say where the gigawatts are to come from, if the page does. Performance figures are Microsoft's claims: attribute them. The second cluster link is a stock explainer: use it for facts about the announcement only. Write your own headline. Dateline Redmond. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: 阿里千问上新AI眼镜！实测用眼睛 “硬控”，2218元起
stories.summary: Alibaba's Qwen has put three AI wearables on sale, and the top model, the N1 Pro glasses at 2,600 yuan, lets the wearer pay by iris: the glasses verify identity from the eye, in a system built with Ant Group and Qualcomm, Zhidx, a mainland Chinese tech outlet, reports after a week with the devices. Lead with payment by iris from a pair of glasses, and the price. The mechanism for a technical reader: say how the three-chip design splits the work (Snapdragon AR1 for imaging, a Bestechnic chip for audio and Bluetooth, a Himax low-power vision chip that keeps the camera sensing all day), what 'always-on environment sensing' does in practice (it starts meeting notes or travel reminders when it recognises the scene), and what the eye tracking and the health sensors in the nose pad collect. The structural point: a camera that never fully sleeps, tied to a payments identity and health data, worn on the face in public; say what Zhidx itself flags as unresolved (accuracy, reliability, protection of payment and health data) and the faults its test found. The claimed false-match rate of under one in a million is Alibaba's figure: attribute it. In Chinese; translate names, prices and specifications exactly and state Zhidx's judgments as its own. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Hangzhou.

stories.label: 11 sailors missing after drone sinks ship off Bulgaria
stories.summary: Two merchant ships were hit by drones about 18 nautical miles off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast in the early hours of Tuesday; one sank and 11 sailors are missing, Prime Minister Rumen Radev said, and Sofia summoned the Russian envoy (Balkan Insight). Lead with the sinking and the missing crew, then the second ship, the Ukrainian-owned, Maltese-flagged Chelsea 3, hit by three drones. Say what is established and what is not: who the crews are and their nationalities, whose drones they were (attribute any blame to whoever states it; give Moscow's and Kyiv's replies), and what the rescue has found. The mechanism: the war at sea has moved into the waters of an EU and NATO member, on the grain and fuel lane that runs down the western Black Sea coast, in the same days an 'energy ceasefire' is supposed to hold; say what it does to insurance and traffic for Bulgarian and Romanian ports and whether Sofia has invoked NATO consultation, only as the pages give it. 'Balkan Insight' says 'new' attacks: give the earlier ones in a clause. TRT World is Turkish state media, used where the others agree. Write your own headline. Dateline Sofia.

stories.label: Trump's right to push a Ukraine-Russia energy cease-fire -- but it must be real
stories.summary: New since Monday's piece on Macron seeing no energy truce on the Russian side (one clause): Kyiv has made a decision. Zelenskyy says Ukraine has halted its strikes on Russian oil refineries for two days (Al Arabiya), while accusing Russia of violating the 'energy ceasefire' Trump announced on Sunday (Al Jazeera). Lead with the two-day halt and its terms: what Ukraine stops hitting, until when, and what it says Russia struck in the meantime. The mechanism: the truce was announced by Washington before either side had agreed its scope, so each now defines it for itself (refineries only, or all energy sites including Ukraine's power grid before winter), and a pause with a deadline is Kyiv's way of putting the burden of proof on Moscow; give Moscow's account. Refinery strikes are Ukraine's main lever on Russian fuel exports, and oil futures fell about 2% as traders priced more Russian diesel reaching the market (News18/PTI): name the price of Brent crude plainly, in one sentence. The feed's lead link is a New York Post editorial: do not write from it beyond the quoted text of Trump's announcement; write from Al Arabiya and Al Jazeera. Sentiment diverges (0.55): say what is established and what is assertion. Write your own headline. Dateline Kyiv.

stories.label: Former DR Congo president Kabila joins M23 rebels in a new coalition
stories.summary: Joseph Kabila, who ruled the Democratic Republic of the Congo for 18 years, has launched a political and military coalition, the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN), that includes the Rwanda-backed M23, the armed group holding Goma and large parts of the east. Lead with that: a former head of state has formally joined the rebellion against his successor, announced at a press conference in rebel-held territory. The mechanism: say who else is in the FRN and what it demands, that a Kinshasa military court sentenced Kabila to death in absentia (the feed tags capital punishment; give the charge and date as the page has them), and what this does to the Washington- and Doha-brokered peace tracks between Kinshasa, Kigali and the M23. Who it lands on: the millions displaced in North and South Kivu, and the miners of the coltan and cobalt both sides finance themselves with. Give President Tshisekedi's government's reply and Rwanda's. No Congolese outlet in the feed carries it. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Goma.

stories.label: Families in Gaza Sleep in Buildings They Know Could Collapse
stories.summary: With most of Gaza's housing damaged or destroyed and reconstruction barely begun, thousands of families are choosing between a tent and a concrete roof that may fall on them. Lead with that choice and the people making it: name the families and buildings the report names, and give any count of collapses and deaths since the ceasefire. The mechanism: say how much of the housing stock is gone (UN figures as the page cites them), why rebuilding has not started (what Israel allows in: cement, steel, heavy machinery; who is meant to pay and administer), and why there is no one to inspect or shore up a damaged building, with winter rain coming. The accountability point: the destruction has a named author and the blockade on materials a named decision-maker; say what Israeli authorities and the bodies overseeing reconstruction answer, or that they did not. It is ground reportage: attribute findings to Inkstick and the people it quotes, and write only what the page supports. No regional outlet in the feed carries it. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Gaza City, or as the report places it.

stories.label: Bancada indígena diminui no Congresso e lideranças se preparam para desmonte e retrocesso
stories.summary: Brazil's elections have shrunk the Indigenous caucus in Congress, and Indigenous leaders say they are preparing for 'dismantling and rollback', Agência Pública reports. Lead with the numbers: how many Indigenous deputies and senators were elected against the outgoing Congress, and who lost their seats. The mechanism: say what the new Congress can do with that arithmetic, in the leaders' own terms: stall land demarcations, impose the Marco Temporal (the rule that Indigenous peoples can claim only land they occupied when the 1988 constitution was signed; say where it stands between the Supreme Court and Congress), and staff Funai, the Indigenous affairs agency, with political appointees. The structural point: demarcated Indigenous land is the Amazon's most effective barrier to deforestation, and the agribusiness bloc that wants it open grew in the same vote; give that bloc's size and its reply if the page has them. In Portuguese; translate names and figures exactly and attribute to Agência Pública and the leaders it quotes. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Brasília.

stories.label: Chip Stocks Tumble on A.I. Spending Fears and Rising Chinese Competition
stories.summary: South Korea's benchmark share index tumbled on Tuesday, led by steep losses in Samsung Electronics and the other memory-chip makers, as two fears met: that spending on artificial intelligence has run ahead of returns, and that Chinese memory makers (the feed tags ChangXin Memory Technologies) are closing on the incumbents. Lead with the Korean fall and its size, then the cause, not the price. The mechanism: memory is the part of the AI build-out that is closest to a commodity, three firms have held it and priced it, and a state-backed Chinese entrant with cleared export hurdles or new capacity breaks that pricing; say what CXMT has announced or shipped, what set off the spending doubts (a company's guidance, an order cut, as the page gives it), and how far the losses spread to Taiwan, Japan and Nasdaq futures. Who it lands on: an economy in which chips are the largest export, and Korean households heavily invested in two stocks. Attribute forecasts to the analysts quoted and state none as fact; no price targets. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Seoul.

stories.label: UK court ruling boosts government's chances of keeping $5 billion in seized bitcoin
stories.summary: A London court has made it likelier that the British state, not the people defrauded, keeps most of some £3.8 billion ($5 billion) in bitcoin seized by the Metropolitan Police. Lead with that: the ruling does not decide ownership, but it narrows the victims' route to recovery, and their lawyers are appealing. The mechanism: say where the coins came from (the fraud, who ran it, how many victims and in which country, as the page gives it), what the victims invested against what the hoard is now worth, and the legal point the court decided: whether victims can claim the appreciated bitcoin or only what they lost, with the difference falling to the Treasury under the Proceeds of Crime Act. The accountability point: a government short of money has a direct interest in the outcome of a case its own prosecutors are arguing. Name the series plainly: the price of bitcoin, whose rise since the seizure is the sum in dispute. CoinDesk is a trade outlet: no price commentary. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline London.

stories.label: Dubai inflation climbs in September as Iran war pushes up fuel cost | The National
stories.summary: Dubai's consumer prices rose 5.03% in the year to September as fuel and transport costs climbed with the Iran war. Lead with the figure and what drove it: give the transport, fuel, housing and food components and the previous month's rate as the page has them. The mechanism: the UAE sets pump prices monthly against world prices, so a Gulf oil exporter's own residents pay the war premium on fuel while the Strait of Hormuz, the emirate's trade route, stays shut; set it beside this morning's IMF cut to Gulf growth forecasts (one clause) and the purchasing managers' survey showing output still rising, and say how the two fit. Who it lands on: the migrant workers who are most of Dubai's population, whose wages are fixed and whose rents are the index's largest weight. Name the series plainly: the price of Brent crude and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The National is the UAE outlet and the only source; it is owned in Abu Dhabi, so attribute the reading of the data to the statistics office and S&P Global. Write your own headline. Dateline Dubai.

stories.label: China-US astronomy team may have found possible relic of a recent 'gold factory'
stories.summary: A Chinese-American team says a mysterious glow in the Milky Way may be the remnant of a recent collision of two neutron stars, the kind of event that forges gold and other heavy elements, and one that may once have shone as brightly as Jupiter in the sky. Lead with the claim and its status together: it is a preprint posted on arXiv last week and has not been peer-reviewed. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what was observed (which telescope, at what wavelengths, how far away and how old the object is estimated to be), why the team reads it as a kilonova remnant and not a supernova remnant, and what observation would confirm or kill the idea. Why it matters: only one neutron-star merger has been seen directly (2017, by gravitational waves, in another galaxy), so a relic in our own galaxy would be the first place to check, up close, where the heavy elements come from. Name the researchers and their institutions, and give an outside astronomer's view if the page has one. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline as the report places the lead institution.

stories.label: Werbeindustrie liest mit: KI-Chatbots schicken Inhalte aus Gesprächen an Tracking-Firmen
stories.summary: Six of nine AI chatbots examined in a study pass information from users' conversations to tracking and advertising services, netzpolitik.org reports, and the well-known ones, ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini, are among those affected. Lead with six of nine and what leaks. The mechanism for a technical reader: say exactly what is transmitted (prompt text, conversation titles, URLs that embed them, identifiers), by what route (third-party analytics scripts and pixels in the web or mobile client), to which companies, and whether it happens for logged-in and paying users; say per product what the study found, and do not generalise from one to all. Name the researchers, their institution and their method, and the three services that sent nothing. The structural point: people tell a chatbot what they would tell a doctor or a lawyer, and it runs on the same ad-tech plumbing as any website; say what the GDPR requires for such transfers and what each company answered. In German; translate exactly, attribute the findings to the study and netzpolitik.org, and state nothing about a product that the study does not. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Berlin.

stories.label: AI labs are buying data from dead startups to train their models
stories.summary: When a startup dies, its Slack messages, design files, code and internal documents are now being sold to AI labs as training data, and a small industry of brokers has formed to arrange it. Lead with the trade and one concrete sale: the founder MIT Technology Review names, what his failed crypto firm's archives fetched, and who bought them. The mechanism for a technical reader: say why labs want it (real records of how work gets done, which the public web does not hold, for training agents), who the brokers are and what they pay, and how the data is cleaned of personal information, if it is. The accountability gap: the employees and customers whose messages are in those archives agreed to nothing, and in a liquidation data is an asset the creditors can sell; say what privacy law, employment contracts and bankruptcy courts do and do not cover, as the piece gives it, and which labs confirmed or declined to comment. Attribute findings to MIT Technology Review. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline as the report places it; US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Tencent Scraps Early Desktop Agent as Platforms Narrow the Field
stories.summary: Tencent will shut QClaw, its early desktop AI agent, before the end of the year and move users to WorkBuddy, TMTPost, a mainland Chinese tech outlet, reports. Lead with the closure and the date. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what QClaw did (an agent that operates the user's own computer) and what WorkBuddy is instead (an office product tied to Tencent's cloud, documents and enterprise systems), and why the general-purpose desktop agent lost: cost per task, reliability, security of handing an agent the whole machine, and no way to charge for it, as the piece gives them. The structural point is the view from inside China's industry: after a spring in which every large platform cloned an agent, the biggest companies are cutting to a few products attached to things enterprises already pay for; name what Alibaba, ByteDance and Baidu have kept or dropped if the page does. One clause on Monday's piece on ByteDance and Tencent answering Meta's Muse agent. Attribute to TMTPost and state its characterisations as its own. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Shenzhen.

stories.label: Anti-Ankara fighters evacuate four bases in Iraq's north
stories.summary: Turkey's intelligence service confirmed on Monday that PKK fighters have withdrawn from four key bases in northern Iraq, the move the group announced last week, two months after Ankara's parliament passed a limited amnesty for its militants. Lead with the confirmation and the four bases (name them and where they are if the page does). The mechanism: a four-decade insurgency that cost some 40,000 lives is being wound down in steps, each side verifying the other: the PKK's dissolution, the amnesty law, now the bases; say what the amnesty covers and excludes, who takes over the vacated ground (Iraqi federal forces, the Kurdistan Region's peshmerga, Turkish troops already inside Iraq), and what Ankara still demands. Who it lands on: villagers in Duhok and Erbil provinces displaced by years of Turkish air strikes, and Kurds in Turkey waiting on the political half of the bargain. Give the PKK's own statement and Baghdad's if the page has them. It is agency copy carried by Dawn; no Turkish or Iraqi outlet in the feed carries it. Single source. Write your own headline, naming the PKK. Dateline Ankara.

stories.label: Scores of PTI workers held in crackdown across KP
stories.summary: New since the 11 October pieces on the emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and the assembly bans in Peshawar, Lahore and Karachi (one clause): the arrests have begun. Scores of PTI workers were detained across the province on Monday, and a case was registered in Swat against two PTI members of the National Assembly, four provincial legislators and dozens of workers over a rally held on 28 September, before the emergency existed. Lead with the detentions (how many, in which districts, on what charges) and the legislators named. The mechanism: governor's rule removed the elected PTI provincial government, and the police and prosecution it controlled now answer to the centre, so old rallies become new cases; the same day the law department dismissed 57 of the province's law officers and appointed 27 (Dawn, https://www.dawn.com/news/2036701 if the writer finds it; otherwise one clause from this page only), and opposition members in the Balochistan Assembly demanded the PTI government be restored (https://www.dawn.com/news/2036756). Give the government's stated grounds and PTI's reply. Dawn is the Pakistani outlet and the only source. Write your own headline, spelling out Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Dateline Peshawar, or Swat if the page is filed from there.

stories.label: Catholics in US Army must not participate in firing squad, prominent archbishop says
stories.summary: Archbishop Timothy Broglio, who oversees the pastoral care of Catholics in the US armed forces, has said Catholic soldiers must not take part in the firing squad for Hasan, the former Army officer who killed 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009, and objected to what Reuters calls an unprecedented plan to broadcast the execution. Lead with the instruction and its target: a senior churchman telling serving soldiers to refuse an order. The mechanism: say what the Army plans (the method, the date, the broadcast and who ordered it, only as the page gives it), that the US military has not executed anyone since 1961, what Catholic teaching on the death penalty has said since 2018, and what military law offers a soldier who refuses on conscience. The reader's stake: the condemned man is a Muslim American whose crime was used for years against Muslims in uniform, and the state now proposes to make his death a broadcast; report that plainly and give the Pentagon's and the victims' families' statements as the page has them. It is Reuters copy carried by Daily Maverick. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Washington. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: UK growth upgraded but energy prices and rates to bite in 2027
stories.summary: New since Sunday's curtain-raiser on the IMF meetings in Bangkok (one clause): the forecasts are out. The IMF's World Economic Outlook raises 2026 world growth to 3.1% while warning that the economy's resilience is waning, and it has sharply cut its 2026 projections for the Gulf economies because the Strait of Hormuz has stayed closed, pushing back the date it assumes the waterway reopens (The National). Lead with that pair, not with Britain: a higher global number beside deep cuts for the exporters whose oil cannot leave. The mechanism: growth this year was pulled forward by investment and stockpiling, and the bill arrives in 2027 as dear energy and higher interest rates bite; give the Gulf figures country by country as The National has them, the old and new assumption on Hormuz, and one sentence on Britain (upgraded for 2026, cut for 2027) from the BBC. Name the series plainly: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, the price of Brent crude and the Fed's interest rate. Who it lands on: Gulf budgets and the migrant workers they pay, and fuel importers in Asia and Africa. These are forecasts: state them as the IMF's. TRT World is Turkish state media, used where the others agree. Write your own headline about the global and Gulf forecasts. Dateline Bangkok.

stories.label: Oil shipping and insurance costs exceed one-third of the commodity value -- OPEC
stories.summary: Ministers of OPEC and its allies say the cost of shipping and insuring oil has reached more than one third of the value of the cargo, a level they call unprecedented and one that is 'impeding' the movement of crude and products. Lead with the fraction: on a barrel near $105, over $35 now goes to freight and war-risk cover before it reaches a refinery. The mechanism: three tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz in two days, the Houthis threaten the Red Sea route, and underwriters reprice every voyage, so the price a producer receives and the price an importer pays have come apart; say what normal freight-and-insurance shares are, as the page gives them, what the ministers asked for or decided, and where they met. Name the series plainly: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and the price of Brent crude. Distinct from Monday's piece on OPEC's demand forecast (one clause). Who it lands on: importers in South Asia and Africa who pay the delivered price, and the seafarers the premium is priced on. The accountability point: several of the ministers' own governments are parties to the war that set the premium. Write from Reuters; TASS is Russian state media, used only for quoted remarks. Write your own headline. Dateline as Reuters places the meeting.

stories.label: Japan's wholesale inflation remains elevated, keeps alive BOJ rate-hike view
stories.summary: Japan's wholesale prices rose 6.8% in the year to September, slower than in August but high enough to keep a near-term Bank of Japan rate rise in view. Lead with the figure and what it measures: the prices companies charge each other, which reach shop shelves months later. The mechanism: Japan imports almost all its energy, much of it through the Strait of Hormuz, and pays for it in a weak yen, so the oil shock and the currency compound in import prices; give the yen-based import price index, the oil and telecoms components and the previous month's figure as the page has them, then the Bank of Japan's current policy rate, its next meeting date and what a rise would do to the yen and to a government carrying the rich world's largest debt. Name the series plainly: the yen and the price of Brent crude. Who it lands on: Japanese households whose wages trail prices. Attribute expectations of a rate rise to the markets and analysts Reuters cites; state none as fact. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Tokyo.

stories.label: 'Pakistan's poverty rate higher than India, B'desh'
stories.summary: More than one third of Pakistan's population lives in multidimensional poverty, overlapping deprivations in health, education and living standards, a higher share than in India or Bangladesh, according to the UNDP's Multidimensional Poverty Index released on Monday. Lead with Pakistan's share and headcount beside its two neighbours' figures.
