The mechanism for a general reader: the index does not count income; it counts households that lack several things at once (a child out of school, a death of a child, no electricity, clean water or cooking fuel), which is why it can diverge from the dollar-a-day measure; say which indicators drive Pakistan's score, how the provinces differ, the survey years behind each country's figure (they differ, and it limits the comparison), and the global totals the report gives for South Asia and sub-Saharan Africa. The structural point: three countries that began from one starting line in 1947 and 1971 have separated on schooling and child survival; give what the report and the Pakistani officials quoted attribute it to, and no more. Attribute all figures to the UNDP. Dawn is the Pakistani outlet and the only source. Write your own headline, spelling out Bangladesh. Dateline as Dawn files it (the report was released in New York); do not count it as a US story.

stories.label: 20个中国品牌挤进巴黎车展，欧洲车企坐不住了
stories.summary: Twenty Chinese car brands are exhibiting at the Paris Motor Show, and TMTPost, a mainland Chinese tech outlet, reports that European carmakers are finding that home advantage is 'becoming less reliable'. Lead with the count and what it was at the last show. The mechanism for a technical reader: say which brands came and with what (battery-electric, plug-in hybrid, range-extender; prices in euros against European rivals; charging speeds, driver-assistance and software the piece cites), how they get round the EU's tariffs on Chinese-made electric cars (hybrids, which the tariff does not cover, and plants in Hungary, Spain or Turkey), and what Renault, Stellantis and Volkswagen showed in answer. One clause on Sunday's China-EU quota deal on hybrids, already covered. The value of this piece is the view from inside China's industry: say how the Chinese makers themselves describe the European market, including overcapacity and the price war at home that pushes them abroad, if the page says so. In Chinese; translate names and figures exactly, attribute to TMTPost, and state its characterisations as its own. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Paris.

stories.label: PAC-3 Edge Will Be The Most Capable Patriot Interceptor Ever
stories.summary: Lockheed Martin has unveiled the PAC-3 Edge, a new interceptor to sit at the top of the Patriot family with more range, altitude and manoeuvrability than the PAC-3 MSE. Lead with what it is and what it is for, stated as the maker's claims. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what changes (motor, seeker, hit-to-kill against which classes of threat: manoeuvring ballistic missiles, hypersonic glide vehicles), whether it fits existing launchers and radars, when it is due and who is paying for development, as the page gives it. The structural point is arithmetic, not performance: Patriot batteries are what stands between Iranian and Houthi missiles and Gulf cities and airports, each interceptor costs millions of dollars against far cheaper attackers, and production of the current round already trails what the Gulf war and Ukraine consume; say what the page gives on output and stockpiles, and that a more capable round is also a costlier and scarcer one. The War Zone is a specialist defence outlet: no performance claim beyond what Lockheed states, attributed. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline as the report places the unveiling. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: Order No. 837: Beijing’s rules for China’s rocket exporters
stories.summary: Beijing has issued Order No. 837, a set of rules governing how China's commercial rocket companies may sell launches and hardware abroad. Lead with the order itself: who issued it, when it takes effect and what it requires of a private launch firm before it can export (licences, state review of customers and technology, as the page gives them). The mechanism for a technical reader: China's 'commercial' launch sector (name the firms the piece names) grew on state engines, state launch sites and provincial money, and the order writes that dependence into export law, so the companies compete for foreign customers as arms of a state system, not as a Chinese SpaceX; say what that means for a buyer in the Gulf, Africa or Southeast Asia choosing between a Chinese launch and an American one under ITAR. One clause on Monday's piece on Kyrgyzstan's satellite only if the page draws a link. The Lowy Interpreter is a think-tank publication and this is analysis: report the order's provisions as facts where the piece documents them, and attribute the reading ('folding entrepreneurial firms into a wider state system') to its author by name. The feed entry is a one-line teaser: read the page first and write only what it supports. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Beijing.
